overview: This bill makes July 20 Lunar Landing Day, an official national observance written into federal law, marking the day in 1969 when astronauts first landed on the Moon. It encourages individuals, organizations and all levels of government to recognize the day with proclamations, activities and educational events that honor the landing and inspire continued U.S. leadership in space exploration and science. It does not create a federal holiday or give anyone a day off. Much of the bill's length simply renumbers and alphabetizes the existing list of national observances in federal law to make room for the new one. The Senate passed it on July 23, 2026, and as of August 20, 2026, it was being held at the desk in the House awaiting action.
for: Supporters say a permanent national day would honor one of the country's greatest achievements and help spark students' interest in science and space.
against: Critics say the designation is symbolic and doesn't change any program or spending, and that adding more official observances does little on its own.
